subject: EverPay integration: adopter handoff & implementation orientation
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aiden Cheng <aiden.cheng@everpay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EverPay integration: adopter handoff & implementation orientation

Hi Aiden —

Thanks again for the thoughtful discovery call last week. This thread is to kick off a short, practical handoff so our CSM/Implementation teams can help your engineers move from POC to production.

High-level plan (30-day orientation):
- Week 0: access + sandbox connectivity checks (API keys, network allowlist)
- Week 1: SDK bootstrap + sample flows (auth, retry patterns, logging)
- Week 2: endpoint migration test (staging -> canary)
- Week 3–4: load sweep + cutover checklist + runbook handoff

I've attached a lightweight checklist (everpay-integration-checklist.xlsx) and a short notes file with recommended SDK snippets (soojin-implementation-notes.txt). Please share the engineering contact who will own the integration repo; copying Vanessa and Monica (CS + Implementation) so we can schedule a 30–45 min tech orientation.

Next actions:
1) Aiden: confirm engineering lead + preferred time window this week for a tech orientation.
2) EverPay: upload sandbox IPs to the allowlist doc (or reply with CIDR).
3) Redwood: we'll surface sample retry/backoff code and a minimal endpoint-migration plan during the call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: everpay-integration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), soojin-implementation-notes.txt (text)

From: Aiden Cheng <aiden.cheng@everpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: dev-support@everpay.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EverPay integration: adopter handoff & implementation orientation

Thanks Soojin — really appreciate the clear plan.

I'll be the engineering lead on this integration. My timeline: we can start the tech orientation on Thursday 18 Mar between 10:00-12:00 PT. Sandbox IPs: 34.82.120.0/24 and 35.196.0.0/20 — I'll ask infra to add Redwood staging.

A few quick notes from our side:
- We prefer language samples in Go and Python; current stack is Go for core payments flows.
- We have a strict 300ms P95 latency goal for checkout auth calls — want to make sure we test tail latency with your recommended SDK batching and fallback.
- We'll likely need guidance on graceful fallback for partial KV cache misses during peak.

I'll attach our short network allowlist confirmation after infra updates.

—
Aiden Cheng
Lead Engineer, Integrations
EverPay
aiden.cheng@everpay.com

Aiden — thanks for the quick reply and for volunteering to lead. Thursday 18 Mar 10:00 PT works for our Implementation lead (Monica) + me. I'll book a 45-minute orientation and include an agenda:

Agenda (45 min):
- 5m introductions & scope
- 10m sandbox connectivity & auth (API keys + allowlist checks)
- 15m SDK bootstrap (Go + Python samples) — we'll demo retry/backoff and KV cache patterns
- 10m endpoint migration plan (staging -> canary -> cutover checklist)
- 5m next steps & owners (runbook handoff, docs)

Pre-reads (please skim if possible):
- everpay-integration-checklist.xlsx (attached earlier)
- soojin-implementation-notes.txt (code snippets + recommended settings)

For the latency goal you mentioned (300ms P95): during the demo we'll show sampling tools and our recommended batching configuration. We recommend starting with these runtime params for your Go SDK:
- max_batch_size: 8
- max_wait_ms: 12
- request_timeout_ms: 600
- retry_policy: exponential (base=100ms, max_backoff=2000ms, attempts=3)

Also: If you'll be running checkout traffic from multiple regions, please flag which region will be primary so we can suggest routing and region-pin strategies.

I'll send a calendar invite in a moment and share a short orientation doc after the call.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Implementation Program Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Aiden — welcome and thanks for the CIDR. Invite is scheduled for Thu 18 Mar 10:00–10:45 PT (Zoom + shared notes).

Quick implementation tips we'll walk through and drop in the runbook after the call:
- SDK bootstrap: include a health-check endpoint that verifies key validity + KV cache warmness on startup. Fail fast on auth errors, but allow degraded mode if cache warm-up is in progress.
- Retries/timeouts: use an idempotency/token approach for POSTs where possible; retries capped to 3 with jitter to reduce thundering herd.
- Rate limit handling: surface 429 with Retry-After when possible; implement local client-side token bucket with burst allowance 2x sustained rate to absorb short spikes.
- Endpoint migration: we recommend a 10% canary for 24 hours, validate p95 latency and error rates against baseline, then 50% for 3 hours before full cutover.

After our orientation we'll provide a simple code bundle (Go + Python) that demonstrates: auth, sample request, retry wrapper, and a short stress script against staging. I'll attach the runbook and drop the zip to the Drive link referenced above.

If anything changes on timing, reply here and we'll adjust. Looking forward to meeting your team.

Best —
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
